title: Electrical control of spin photocurrent in a magnetoelectric oxide Cr$_2$O$_3$
abstract: Controlling magnetism by electric field or current is a central topic in spintronics. In this work, we argue that the magnon spin photocurrent can also be controlled by the electric field in magnetoelectrics. Taking Cr$_2$O$_3$ as an example, we demonstrate how the spin current is modified by the electric field, using nonlinear response theory. We find that the Dzyaloshinsky--Moriya interaction induced by the applied field plays a key role in modifying spin-current conductivity, which exhibits pronounced anisotropy with respect to the light polarization. In particular, both the resonance frequency and the peak intensity show distinct dependences on the external electric field $E$, demonstrating electrical control of the spin photocurrent. In addition, we show that the two-magnon processes give rise to a continuum spectrum, a consequence of the field-induced spin canting. These results show that Cr$_2$O$_3$ is a promising platform for realizing electrically tunable spin photovoltaic effect.
summary: The paper theoretically investigates the electrical control of magnon spin photocurrent in the magnetoelectric oxide $	ext{Cr}_2	ext{O}_3$. Using nonlinear response theory, the authors show that an applied electric field modifies the spin current conductivity via the Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction. The results confirm that this material is a promising platform for electrically tunable optospintronic devices.
main_problem: The study investigates how an applied electric field can electrically control the magnon spin photocurrent generated in magnetoelectric oxides.
main_result: The research demonstrates that the Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction, induced by the electric field, significantly modifies the spin-current conductivity, confirming electrical tunability of this effect.
method: Nonlinear response theory is employed to calculate the second-order nonlinear spin current conductivity ($\sigma^{(2)}$), decomposing it into one-magnon and two-magnon contributions.
model_or_system: The physical system studied is $	ext{Cr}_2	ext{O}_3$, modeled using 1D and 3D spin chain Hamiltonians that incorporate nearest-neighbor exchange, Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction (DMI), and anisotropy terms.
key_observables: Nonlinear spin current conductivity ($\sigma^{(2)}$) components for different polarizations ($z_{xx}, z_{yy}$, etc.), resonance frequencies, and continuum spectrum features.
important_parameters: Applied electric field ($E$), magnon frequency ($\Omega$), temperature (analyzed at $T=0$ in some parts), and exchange coupling constants ($J$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the linear spin-wave approximation for the magnon Hamiltonian, and certain calculations assume zero temperature or slow variation of matrix elements near resonance.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematic models of spin chains with canting (Fig. 1), show $\sigma^{(2)}$ spectra for one-magnon and two-magnon processes in 1D (Fig. 2, Fig. 3), and present the magnon dispersion relations for $	ext{Cr}_2	ext{O}_3$ (Fig. 4).
paper_structure: The paper builds from general theory using nonlinear response formalism to specific calculations on 1D and 3D spin models, analyzing both one-magnon resonance peaks and the two-magnon continuum spectrum as functions of the external electric field.
why_interesting: This work bridges concepts from spintronics (spin currents), multiferroics (magnetoelectric coupling), and advanced many-body theory (nonlinear response/bosonic excitations), providing a theoretical framework for electrically controlling quantum magnetic responses.
